How Many Shares of AT&T, Comcast or Verizon Pay $1,000 a Month in Dividends?
sum: - At today’s prices, $1,000 a month in dividends takes 10,811 shares of AT&T, 9,091 shares of Comcast or 4,241 shares of Verizon.
- Verizon’s 6.1% yield makes it the cheapest of the three by about $43,000, and its check is the one I’d want.
- Verizon pays out the biggest share of its free cash flow, 52% over the last 12 months, but that still leaves plenty of room, and its free cash flow is growing.
- Comcast covers its dividend with the most room, but its split into two companies, due by the middle of next year, leaves its dividend plans open.

For a hypothetical retiree who wants a $1,000 monthly dividend check from a single stock, AT&T (T), Comcast (CMCSA) and Verizon Communications (VZ) can all deliver. They just charge very different prices for it.

At today’s prices, Verizon’s 6.1% yield gets there with 4,241 shares, or about $197,600. Comcast takes 9,091 shares at a 5.3% yield, about $227,500, and AT&T, yielding 5.0%, takes 10,811 shares, about $240,700.

Is Verizon (NYSE:VZ) Leaning on Fiber and AI?
sum: - The carrier is widening fiber and cloud agreements aimed at carrying artificial-intelligence traffic across long-haul routes.
- Dividend consistency remains central to how the telecom group is viewed among steady payout names.
- Network modernization is reshaping the narrative around the stock as demand for data capacity climbs.

Recent agreements with a major cloud provider and with leading optical-fiber suppliers have framed a story that reaches well beyond the quarter-to-quarter rhythm of phone additions, touching instead the backbone that moves information between data centers across the country. The wireless and broadband arena in the country remains a contest among a small number of national carriers, each spending heavily to modernize its reach and defend its base of connections. Competition on price, device promotions, and bundled broadband has stayed intense, and the group that can convert spending into durable connections tends to earn steadier footing with the market. Layered onto that familiar rivalry is a newer theme: the role carriers can play in the data-center era. Optical fiber has become a prized asset as computing demand surges, and the firms that control dense, long-haul routes are being drawn into agreements that connect sprawling server campuses. That shift has nudged the sector narrative from purely consumer-facing metrics toward the plumbing that underpins the broader digital economy.

T-Mobile, Verizon Or AT&T: Which US Wireless Carrier Makes The Most Sense For SpaceX To Buy?
sum: Shares of SpaceX (SPCX) rose 6% on Monday, extending their winning streak to two sessions, as Barclays said T-Mobile US (TMUS) could offer the strongest strategic fit if Elon Musk pursues a major wireless acquisition. As SpaceX prepares to launch its own nationwide terrestrial 5G network in 2027, Barclays believes acquiring an established carrier could help accelerate that ambition.
SPCX stock jumped to $142.07 on Monday, posting its second consecutive session in the green.
Barclays said U.S. carriers face a trade-off: selling spare network capacity to SpaceX could bring in revenue while helping a future rival.

“That is the prisoner’s dilemma we have highlighted in our prior notes as, individually, each incumbent benefits from monetizing unused network capacity through wholesale but, collectively, they benefit from denying SpaceX terrestrial access,” the brokerage said, according to Barron’s.
For SpaceX, buying a carrier could offer a faster route into consumer wireless than negotiating access and building operations from scratch.

“A major carrier acquisition would simultaneously solve spectrum, [technical issues], roaming, retail/distribution, handset relationships, customer care, device financing and, most importantly, time,” the firm said. “That would make buying increasingly attractive if SpaceX’s objective really is a large-scale consumer mobile business.”
Barclays called T-Mobile the “strategically cleanest Big Three combination,” citing its lower rural share as a natural complement to Starlink’s strength in those areas.

items.t: VZ Shares Rise 14.7% in a Year: What's the Next Move for Investors?
sum: Verizon Communications Inc.VZ has increased 14.7% in a year compared with the Wireless National industry’s growth of 105.6%. The stock has outformed the Zacks Computer & Technology sector during this period.
The company has outperformed its peers like AT&T Inc.T and T-Mobile US, Inc.TMUS. Shares of AT&T have declined 12.9%, while T-Mobile has declined 21.3% during this period.

AI infrastructure represents an emerging source of revenue diversification for Verizon. The company has signed a dark fiber agreement worth more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services (AWS), building on its earlier agreement with Google to connect AI data centers. Management disclosed approximately $4 billion in signed contracts, supported by growing demand from hyperscalers, neocloud providers and enterprise customers.

Intensifying competition in the U.S. wireless and broadband markets remains a significant concern for Verizon. The company faces strong competition from AT&T, T-Mobile and cable operators, which continue to use competitive pricing, promotional incentives and bundled offerings to attract subscribers. Although Verizon has recently improved customer acquisition and retention metrics, sustaining subscriber growth without increasing promotional spending will be important. Its strategy of competing through network quality, customer experience and value-added services rather than aggressive price discounts could help protect margins. However, competitors adopting similar convergence strategies or increasing promotional activity could put pressure on Verizon's subscriber growth and pricing flexibility.

Weakness in equipment revenue is another challenge for the company. While mobility and broadband service revenue increased 2.9% year over year to $23.5 billion in the third quarter, lower equipment sales limited overall revenue growth. Total revenue increased just 1.5% to $34.3 billion, as equipment revenue declined 9% year over year. Management attributed the decline primarily to a reduction in wireless device upgrade activity, with postpaid upgrade volumes falling 20.3% from the prior-year quarter.
Verizon's substantial investment requirements and elevated debt remain important considerations.

Verizon (NYSE:VZ | VZ Price Prediction) pays a 6.22% dividend yield, even after shares rose 19.82% year to date. A yield that high often signals the market expects a cut, the same red flags we cataloged in a free dividend trap guide. Verizon’s latest cash flow numbers suggest the payout is on solid ground.

Verizon generated $18 billion of free cash flow in the first nine months of 2026, up 14.3%. Over the same period, it paid $8.8 billion in dividends, so the payout used about 49% of free cash flow. Verizon Q3 Revenue Falls Short of Wall Street as Shares Slide 3.5%
sum: Verizon Communications Inc. (VZ) posted third-quarter revenue that fell short of analyst estimates, sending the telecom carrier's shares down 3.49% to close at $43.10 on Monday after an intraday drop of nearly 5% to $43.84.

The New York-based company reported revenue of $34.31 billion for the July-September period, up 1.5% from a year earlier but below the roughly $34.85 billion consensus. Adjusted diluted earnings per share rose about 8% to $1.31, topping the $1.27 analysts had expected. Net income climbed 5.2% to $5.32 billion.

The top-line miss overshadowed what management described as a record quarter on several fronts. Wireless service revenue, spanning consumer and business customers, grew 2.9% to $23.49 billion. Verizon added 406,000 postpaid phone subscribers, an increase of more than 820% year over year and its strongest third-quarter showing in five years. Postpaid net accounts rose by 137,000, the best result in more than a decade.

"Verizon delivered another record-breaking quarter. One year into our transformation, Verizon is fundamentally stronger - operationally, financially, and competitively," Chief Executive Dan Schulman said. "By prioritizing customer-first offerings like Simplicity and our expanded loyalty program over heavy subsidies, we are winning loyal, high-value customers while expanding margins, reducing churn, and generating strong sustained cash flow."

Consolidated adjusted EBITDA reached $13.8 billion, up 8.0% from a year earlier, which the company called its highest quarterly figure on record. Cash flow from operations rose 2.2% to $11.5 billion, supporting free cash flow of $7.8 billion, a 12.1% increase.
Verizon also disclosed an expanded artificial intelligence infrastructure agreement with Amazon Web Services valued at more than $2 billion, deepening a partnership with Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN).

For the full year, Verizon lifted its adjusted EPS guidance for the third consecutive quarter, to $5.04-$5.06 from $4.99-$5.04, implying growth of 7.0% to 7.5% versus the prior 6.0%-7.0% range. The midpoint of $5.05 sits above the $5.02 consensus. The company now expects 1.1 million to 1.2 million postpaid phone net additions, up from the upper half of its earlier 750,000-to-1-million range - more than triple the 2025 target.

‘Real consequences’: AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile warn FCC as Elon Musk plots a SpaceX phone network for the US by 2028
sum: AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile have spent months insisting a satellite company can't compete with their networks. Investors aren't convinced.

On Oct. 23, shares of AT&T (NYSE:T) and T-Mobile (NASDAQ:TMUS) each fell nearly 8% after Bloomberg reported that SpaceX is in talks to access at least 80,000 U.S. cell sites, a step toward becoming the country's fourth nationwide carrier. Verizon (NYSE:VZ) slipped about 1.2%.

The selloff came a day after the carriers' trade group, CTIA, filed a letter with the Federal Communications Commission following Oct. 20 meetings with agency officials. In it, CTIA warned that "the Commission's buildout decisions have real consequences for consumers who rely on ever-increasing wireless capacity to access the modern economy and support their day-to-day living."

The letter doesn't mention SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX), which wants to become one of those carriers. On the company's Oct. 20 earnings call, President Gwynne Shotwell said a new spectrum purchase and the FCC's approval of its next satellites would "pave the way" for Starlink Mobile to become a major U.S. mobile carrier, with service on its own airwaves targeted for early 2028. Musk told analysts he sees "a clear path to several hundred billion dollars a year" in connectivity revenue, from a business that brought in about $5.2 billion in the third quarter.

The U.S. hasn't had four national carriers since T-Mobile bought Sprint in 2020. Regulators approved the deal expecting Dish Network to build a fourth network. The plan fell apart in 2025, when Dish's parent, EchoStar, agreed to sell spectrum to AT&T for about $23 billion and to SpaceX in deals now worth about $19.6 billion, and moved its Boost Mobile customers onto AT&T's network. The FCC approved AT&T's purchase and SpaceX's in May.

Verizon Shares Fall 5.4% After SpaceX Spectrum Deal Raises Competition Concerns
sum: Verizon Communications (NYSE:VZ) shares declined 5.4% to $43.20 in premarket trading on Friday after SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) announced an agreement to acquire a nationwide portfolio of wireless spectrum, raising concerns about increased competition in the US telecommunications market.

SpaceX confirmed on Thursday evening that it had entered into a definitive agreement to purchase 100% of Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz low-band spectrum portfolio, comprising up to 14 megahertz of paired frequencies.

The transaction, valued at approximately $8 billion, could support the expansion of Starlink Mobile's satellite-to-phone services and provide additional spectrum resources for developing a broader mobile communications network.
SpaceX Chief Executive Elon Musk described the acquisition as the final critical component needed to deliver comprehensive mobile phone coverage across the United States.
The announcement prompted selling across established telecommunications operators as investors assessed the potential implications for their longer-term competitive positions.
SpaceX Acquisition Could Expand Starlink Mobile's Network Capabilities

The 800 MHz spectrum is particularly valuable for mobile communications because lower-frequency signals can travel relatively long distances and penetrate buildings more effectively than higher-frequency alternatives.

sum: SpaceX announced an agreement on Thursday to purchase a nationwide spectrum portfolio as it pushes its Starlink service deeper into the U.S. telecommunications market.

The deal involves the acquisition of a spectrum portfolio from Grain Management, which specializes in digital infrastructure, and is subject to approval by the Federal Communications Commission. SpaceX said in a statement that it's a "license portfolio of up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band."
"This prime low-band spectrum addresses one of the key remaining technical gaps that will pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major mobile carrier in the US," SpaceX said.
In a post on X, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk called it a "very big deal."

Last week, T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon formed a joint venture "focused on expanding coverage in underserved areas," via satellite and direct-to-device (D2D) services, and Starlink was notably absent. T-Mobile has also previously removed mention of Starlink from its T-Satellite promotions.
SpaceX appears determined to battle telecommunications giants in the U.S., and deliver its own services without them.

sum: Verizon Communications Inc (NYSE:VZ, XETRA:BAC) shares rose about 3% on Friday morning after the company reported second quarter results that beat Wall Street expectations for adjusted earnings and raised its full-year outlook, despite revenue coming in below forecasts.
The company reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.30 for the quarter ended June 30, ahead of analyst estimates of $1.27 to $1.28.
Total revenue was $34.25 billion, slightly below expectations of about $35.28 billion.

Mobility and broadband service revenue increased 2.8% year over year to approximately $23.4 billion, with Verizon forecasting growth to accelerate to around 4% in the fourth quarter of 2026. The company added more than 550,000 total mobility and broadband connections during the quarter, more than double the level from the first half of 2025.

Broadband net additions totaled 348,000 in the second quarter, including 193,000 fixed wireless access additions and 155,000 fiber broadband additions. Verizon said it now has approximately 17.1 million fixed wireless access and fiber broadband connections.
Following the results, Verizon raised its full-year guidance, now expecting mobility and broadband service revenue growth of 2.5% to 3.0% in 2026.
The company also lifted its adjusted EPS outlook to $4.99 to $5.04, representing year-over-year growth of 6% to 7%, and increased its full-year share buyback target to up to $4.5 billion.

sum: BT and Verizon have agreed to combine their international operations into a 50:50 joint venture. The new entity will have a combined annual revenue of around $4bn and serve around 3,000 multinational organisations.
BT will receive a $0.6bn payment from Verizon as part of the transaction.
The transaction is expected to complete in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

As a result of the transaction, BT has trimmed its full-year revenue guidance by around £2bn to £17.1-17.6bn. Underlying cash profit (EBITDA) is now expected to be £8.1-8.2bn, slightly lower than previously guided.

BT’s spin-off of its international business marks a key step in streamlining the business and refocusing its efforts on domestic operations. The new international business will be half-owned by both BT and Verizon and is expected to benefit from greater scale and operational efficiencies as the two companies combine their international divisions.

BT’s wider strategy involves significantly modernising and simplifying operations and product lines. That includes bringing the BT brand back into parts of the consumer offering, while continuing to move customers onto the new 5G and fibre broadband networks, which have lower running costs than legacy infrastructure. Fewer repairs, better customer journeys and network efficiencies are also helping to support profits.

Cost cuts remain a long-term focus, with management now targeting a leaner workforce by the end of the decade and raising the overall transformation savings plan. There should also be a further benefit from lower investment as the heaviest phase of the fibre build passes. That’s good news for future cash flows, with BT reiterating its target for free cash flow to rise to around £2bn in 2027 and around £3bn by the end of the decade. That should help support the 4.4% prospective dividend yield as well as ongoing efforts to strengthen the balance sheet. There are no guarantees.

sum: Verizon Communications, Inc. VZ and Charter Communications CHTR are both prominent players in the U.S. telecom sector. The companies primarily compete in fixed broadband, wireless services and enterprise connectivity verticals.

Verizon offers communication services in the form of local phone service, long-distance calls, wireless and data services. Charter Communications is the second largest cable operator in the United States and a leading broadband communications company providing video, Internet and voice services.

The U.S. telecom sector is highly competitive and saturated. Growing usage of high-bandwidth applications, surging AI workloads and federal initiatives to foster digital inclusivity are primarily driving investment in this domain. Amid this backdrop, let us analyze in depth the competitive strengths and weaknesses of the companies to understand who is in a better position to maximize gains from the emerging market trends.

Charter is benefiting from solid momentum in the Mobile Business. Charter added 428,000 mobile lines in the fourth quarter of 2025. It ended the year with 11.8 million total mobile lines, up 19.4% YoY. Mobile service revenues rose 13.1% year over year to $973 million.

To improve churn, the company has introduced bundled plans. Revenues from residential connectivity, including broadband + mobile, increased 2.3% year over year in the fourth quarter of 2025. The company boasts a massive network footprint consisting of 58.4 million fiber passings, 1 million-plus network miles and more than 300K fiber lit buildings. It is also planning to upgrade to symmetrical and multi-gigabit speeds across its footprint by 2027. Charter is committed to investing $7 billion to add 100,000+ miles of fiber-optic network infrastructure. The goal is to deliver symmetrical and multi-gigabit Internet services across 1.7 million locations. Charter activated 483,000 subsidized rural passings in 2025.

However, the company faces stiff competition from other major players such as AT&T, Inc. T and Verizon. The company is rapidly expanding its fiber reach to build a national broadband platform. It has taken multiple approaches to realize this objective. VZ currently has 30 million fiber passings with a target of reaching 40-50 million fiber passings in the medium term. Verizon will add at least 2 million fiber passings in 2026. Alongside this organic fiber buildout, the company is also opting for strategic acquisitions to expand its fiber footprint.

In the first quarter of 2026, Verizon secured all the regulatory approvals needed to close the acquisition of Frontier Communications. The acquisition will boost Verizon’s reach across 31 states in the country. Along with fiber expansion, the acquisition also supports Verizon’s convergence strategy and brings several cross-selling opportunities.

Frontier customers will gain from Verizon’s premium mobility, home Internet, streaming and connected home offerings. Verizon’s wireless customers will have access to Frontier’s premium broadband offerings. VZ is set to launch enticing bundled mobile and home internet plans for customers. Users tied to multiple services are less likely to move away from their existing service provider. In a highly competitive and saturated U.S. telecom market, this prudent strategy for Verizon will likely improve churn rate.

To gain a competitive edge in the industry, Verizon is also focusing on diversifying its revenue base. It is venturing into the automotive market with innovative product launches such as Edge Transportation Exchange. This is a state-of-the-art mobile-network vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication platform for connected vehicles. Such a strong focus on innovation and expansion into other emerging markets bodes well for sustainable growth.

Verizon's overall revenue rose 2% year over year to $36.4 billion, with service revenue edging up 0.1% to $28.2 billion and wireless equipment revenue climbing 9.1% to $8.2 billion.

Consumer revenue increased by 3.2% year over year to $28.14 billion, with service revenue up 0.9%. The company's business unit continued to lag, with revenue decreasing by 1.8% year over year to $7.4 billion, as wireline customers continue to churn off.
Overall adjusted EPS slipped by 0.9% to $1.09, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) fell 0.6% to $11.9 billion.

Verizon also announced a huge $25 billion buyback to be completed over the next three years, while reiterating its commitment to its dividend. This will be backed by its strong free cash flow, which the company sees climbing by 7% next year to $21.5 billion. At the same time, it plans to keep its unsecured leverage (net unsecured net/adjusted EBITDA) between 2 times and 2.25 times to maintain its balance sheet strength.

Verizon has decided it will no longer be the wireless company that others steal customers from, and its net additions in Q4 were impressive. Meanwhile, with the closing of the acquisition of Frontier Communications, Verizon has a big cross-selling and bundling opportunity in front of it.

The dividend looks secure, being well covered by Verizon's free cash flow, while the buyback should help lend support to its lagging stock price. Even after the stock's post-earnings jump, it still trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 9.2 times based on 2026 earnings estimates, compared to an 11.3 times multiple for rival AT&T. With a 6.5% forward yield, Verizon is a solid dividend stock to still buy.
